name: Phone charger
summary: Modern phone chargers commonly support a wide input-voltage range.
guidance: Read the charger's input label and look for a range such as 100–240 V, 50/60 Hz. A plug adapter may still be required.

name: Laptop
summary: Laptop power supplies commonly accept both major voltage systems.
guidance: Confirm the power supply input label includes the destination voltage and frequency. The detachable mains lead may need an adapter.

name: Camera charger
summary: Many camera battery chargers are designed for international voltage ranges.
guidance: Check the exact charger's input label for the destination voltage and frequency; do not infer compatibility from the camera model.

name: Hair dryer
summary: Hair dryers are high-power devices and are often made for one voltage system.
guidance: Use only at a voltage explicitly supported on the rating label. A small electronic travel converter is usually not suitable for this load.

name: Hair straightener
summary: Voltage support varies significantly between hair straightener models.
guidance: Check the rating label or manual for the full input range. Plug fit alone does not show whether the heating appliance is voltage-compatible.

name: Electric toothbrush
summary: Electric toothbrush charging bases do not all support worldwide voltages.
guidance: Check the charging base, not only the toothbrush, for its voltage and frequency rating. Some bases require a voltage-specific replacement.

name: Gaming console
summary: Power-supply design and voltage support differ between console models and revisions.
guidance: Use the rating on the console or its external power supply. Also check regional warranty and display-system considerations before travel.

name: CPAP machine
summary: CPAP power requirements must be confirmed for the exact machine and accessories.
guidance: Follow the manufacturer's travel guidance and rating label, including humidifier and battery requirements. Arrange a reliable backup for essential use.
